name: Alma
one_liner: Search a directory of therapists who take your insurance, book a free consultation, and pay your copay per session.
best_for: People with commercial insurance (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, some Blue Cross plans) who want therapy for their copay
People who want to choose a therapist by identity or specialty and try a free consultation first
People who want in-person sessions with some therapists
People paying out of network who want a therapist offering a sliding scale
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who mainly need medication management (Alma is mainly a therapy directory)
People who do not want advertising trackers on a therapy website
short_description: A directory of independent therapists, many in network with commercial insurance; you book and pay your copay or the therapist's rate.
long_description: Alma is a US network of independent licensed therapists who pay Alma a membership and can bill insurance through it. You search its directory by insurance, state, specialty and identity, book a free consultation, and see the therapist by video or in person. Each provider sets their own rates and decides whether to go in network. In network, you pay your plan's copay or coinsurance; Alma's cost estimator works for plans including Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, Oxford, Optum, Oscar and UnitedHealthcare. Out of network, you pay the therapist's rate, which Alma says is usually $130 to $380 a session, and many therapists offer a sliding scale or out-of-network care. Alma does not accept Medicaid; Medicare acceptance is limited. Alma acts as a HIPAA business associate for your health records, but its website privacy notice says it takes part in advertising networks that track you across sites.
patient_summary: You search Alma's directory by insurance, state and specialty, book a free consultation with a therapist, and then meet by video or in person. If the therapist is in network with your plan, you pay your copay or coinsurance; otherwise you pay the therapist's own rate, which Alma says usually falls between $130 and $380 a session, and some offer a sliding scale. Alma mainly works with commercial plans, not Medicaid.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; therapist's own rate self-pay (Alma says usually $130–$380/session)
pricing.notes: No fee to clients; therapists pay Alma a membership. In network you pay your plan's copay or coinsurance. Each therapist sets their own self-pay rate; many offer a sliding scale, and supervised interns may charge less. Free initial consultation. Cost estimator available for some insurers.

privacy.notes: Privacy notice says Alma participates in advertising networks that track your activity across sites, and its cookie banner offers an opt-out of 'sale'; you can request deletion of data it collected (health records via your provider); Alma is a HIPAA business associate for health records.

seo.title: Alma: Find a Therapist Who Takes Your Insurance
seo.meta_description: Alma helps you find therapists who accept your insurance, with most sessions costing just your copay of $0-50.

faqs.a: Alma is free to search and book—you only pay your insurance copay, typically $0-50 per session. There's no platform fee or subscription. Some providers also offer out-of-network services with superbills for potential reimbursement.

Alma providers accept most major insurance including Aetna, Cigna, BCBS, UnitedHealthcare, Oxford, Oscar, and many state Medicaid plans. Coverage varies by provider and state. Enter your insurance details to see in-network options.

faqs.q: How is Alma different from Headway?
faqs.a: Both connect patients with insurance-accepting therapists. Alma is known for provider diversity and LGBTQ+ affirming care. Headway has a larger overall network. Both are free to use—you only pay your copay. Try both to compare available providers.

Alma focuses primarily on therapy rather than psychiatry. If you need medication management, consider platforms like Cerebral, Teladoc, or Headway which include psychiatric providers. Alma therapists can coordinate with external prescribers.

primary_uses: Video or in-person therapy billed to insurance
Out-of-network therapy with a sliding-scale option

availability.note: US only, all 50 states; mostly commercial insurance. Medicaid not accepted; Medicare limited.
